changes_made.explanation: Removed 'Text Summarization' as the paper is specifically about data-to-text generation of exam results, not summarization tasks
No automatic metrics were mentioned or used in the paper
No LLMs were used as judges in this paper (published before LLM-as-judge became common)

guideline: Participants stated whether results were good/bad for the student (Yes/No/Maybe)
Participants rated preference between hedged and non-hedged texts on Likert scale from -3 (Text A) to +3 (Text B)
Participants provided free-text comments explaining their choices
Participants stated goodness of results (Yes/No/Maybe) and text preference using a Likert scale, with free-text comments

participants were asked to state whether they felt the results were good or not for the student (Yes, No, Maybe) and a preference between the two texts A and B. This was done using a Likert scale which ran from -3 for Text A to +3 for Text B. If both texts were considered by a participant to be the same then a score of 0 was given. The participants were asked to provide free text comments on why they made their particular choice of text.

changes_made.explanation: Condensed redundant guideline descriptions into a single clear guideline and normalized terminology

overall_notes: The paper is a reproduction study focused on human evaluation of hedged vs non-hedged data-to-text generation. It does not involve automatic evaluation or LLM judges. The human evaluation methodology is clearly described with preference ratings and qualitative feedback.
